title: Adaptive navigation silently discards per-navigation arguments
root_cause: navigate(route, arguments) appends only the route String. No entry or argument payload is stored; the host passes the graph destination's static Map<String, NavArgument> definition to content instead of a navigation entry's values.
impact: Callers cannot send different argument values to two visits of the same route. The API accepts input that is never observed; saved/restored stacks likewise carry no arguments. The module is currently unpublished, which limits consumer exposure but not the defect.
recommendation: Before stabilizing or publishing navigation, define a typed entry/payload contract distinct from argument schema; validate and merge defaults at navigation, expose resolved values to content, and implement a save/restore policy. Preserve or deprecate the current overload explicitly rather than silently dropping inputs.
risks: Changing public types and saver format affects callers and restoration; do not hide the change in the identity migration. Never persist secrets or arbitrary unserializable objects by default.
required_tests: Navigate to one route with two distinct payloads; each visit receives its own values.
Validate missing, nullable, wrong-type and defaulted arguments.
Round-trip entry IDs and arguments through the saver; reject unsupported values predictably.
evidence: All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.

Host line43 calls destination.content(destination.arguments); there is no lookup of the navigate arguments parameter.
No route interpolation/deep-link argument parser is wired into AdaptiveNavHost.

title: Route-keyed saved state aliases duplicate back-stack entries and incompletely fixes #542
root_cause: The stack permits duplicate strings, but the state provider key is currentDestination (route) and popped-state cleanup compares sets of routes. There is no unique navigation-entry identity.
impact: A -> B -> A reuses the first A's saveable state; A -> A can keep the same composition. Popping one occurrence while another remains cannot discard only the popped entry's state. A pop/re-push between observed compositions is also invisible to route-set cleanup.
recommendation: Give each stack entry a stable unique ID, key state and cleanup by that ID, persist it with the entry, and prune state for removed entries. Retain the positive distinct-route behavior introduced by #542.
risks: Saver compatibility and lifecycle expectations must be specified. A route-key optimization is not equivalent to Jetpack Navigation's per-entry owners. Compose/device reproduction remains required; this finding is based on the explicit identity algorithm.
required_tests: A -> B -> A has two independent counters and popping restores the original A.
Consecutive A -> A produces fresh local/saveable entry state.
Pop and immediately push the same route before an idle frame; the new entry is fresh.
Restore a stack containing duplicate routes and pop each independently.
Retain both existing #542 tests.

title: NavArgument builder rejects missing/null defaults and accepts mismatched typed defaults
root_cause: build() unconditionally requires defaultValue != null, even if a type was supplied, and NavArgument stores defaultValue as non-null Any. setDefaultValue accepts Any? but build never verifies compatibility with the declared type.
impact: A valid typed required argument without a default cannot be constructed; a nullable String argument cannot explicitly default to null. An Int type with a String default builds and then throws ClassCastException from putDefaultValue. The missing-required-arguments helper cannot be reached through a normal default-absent builder configuration.
recommendation: Represent default absence separately from an explicit null; permit declared types without defaults; reject incompatible defaults at construction and handle nullable defaults consistently. Keep required-argument detection separate from per-value verification.
risks: Avoid relying on unchecked generic casts or platform-specific reflection to implement common type validation. Existing callers might rely on delayed failure, so document the fail-fast change.
required_tests: Typed Int without default builds and is required.
Nullable String with explicit null builds and retains defaultValuePresent=true.
Nonnullable Int with null or String default rejects at build, not later.
All built-in scalar and array defaults, missing-required predicate and verify behavior are covered on JVM/JS/Wasm/Native.

title: AdaptiveBundle violates documented runtime type and fallback contracts
root_cause: The generic get uses an erased as? T without a reified/type-token check, so JVM caller casts can throw despite the documented null-on-wrong-type behavior. getString calls toString on any value. putObject recognizes fewer types than the bundle's explicit setters, including omission of Float.
impact: A wrong-type lookup may crash or silently coerce data rather than returning null/default. Generic insertion rejects values that explicit insertion supports. These inconsistencies impede reliable argument validation and migrations.
recommendation: Use well-defined typed accessors or a portable checked type strategy; align getString with its contract; decide and test the supported generic put set. Document this as an in-memory mutable map, not an Android Parcelable/PersistableBundle replacement.
risks: Array/list values and mMap are exposed mutable references; deep-copy/thread-safety semantics are not currently provided. Kotlin/JS and Native generic-cast behavior must be tested rather than inferred from the JVM run.
required_tests: Wrong-type get<Int> from a String follows the chosen contract without an unexpected caller ClassCastException.
getString of Int42 returns the documented fallback/null rather than "42".
All explicitly supported scalar/array/list setters have consistent generic insertion and retrieval rules.
Explicit null versus absent key, aliasing and mutation behavior are documented/tested.
evidence: All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
Baseline JVM checks reproduce wrong-type generic-get ClassCastException, Int-to-String coercion and putObject(Float) rejection.
Specific primitive getters instead use explicit as? checks with default fallback, e.g. getDouble lines551-553.

title: AdaptiveNavType inference and serialization are incomplete and not reliably round-trippable
root_cause: String-array inference is commented out even though StringArrayType exists; custom Parcelable/Serializable lookup is entirely commented. String serialization leaves URI delimiters unescaped despite its KDoc, uses "null" for null and literal "null", and arrays inherit object toString serialization rather than an array codec.
impact: Supported explicit String arrays fail inferred construction; string values lose distinctions on parse/serialize and can violate a caller's URI encoding expectations. Array serialized values cannot be used to reconstruct the original arrays. These are helper-API defects, not an active deep-link injection exploit: the host does not currently parse routes.
recommendation: Specify a small portable type/codec contract, implement consistent inference including String arrays, define null versus literal encoding and round-trip serialization, and remove unsupported Parcelable/XML claims. If URI encoding belongs in another layer, state that clearly and change the misleading contract.
risks: Encoding changes can break stored routes and must not double-encode already encoded data. Adding runtime reflection to common code would sacrifice multiplatform compatibility. Repeated array parseValue(previous) calls allocate copies and are O(n²) across n values.
required_tests: StringArray inference succeeds for empty and nonempty arrays and rejects mixed arrays.
Round-trip null, literal "null", Unicode, slash/query/hash/ampersand characters and every supported array type.
Unknown/custom fromArgType fails with a truthful supported-types error.
Benchmark/bound repeated-array parsing before adopting it for large external inputs.

title: AdaptiveNavHost retains stale graph closures and does not initialize a replacement controller
root_cause: The graph builder is remembered without keys, and initialization is a LaunchedEffect(Unit). Recomposition with another controller, startDestination or builder does not rebuild graph closures or rerun start-route setup.
impact: Replacing an empty controller at the same composition location can render no destination indefinitely; remembered destination lambdas can still capture the previous controller or stale state. Callers cannot infer the graph lifetime contract from the signature.
recommendation: Choose and document static versus dynamic graph ownership. Key controller initialization correctly; use stable graph specifications and updated callback/state capture or intentional graph keys. Add replacement tests before exposing navigation as supported.
risks: Blindly keying on an unstable builder lambda may rebuild the graph on every recomposition and lose state. Changing startDestination must not unexpectedly reset an existing stack.
required_tests: Replace a controller at one composition site and verify initialization and callback routing.
Recompose after an outer callback/state changes and confirm graph content sees intended values.
Change startDestination with an empty and nonempty stack under an explicit policy.
evidence: All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.

title: Unknown routes and duplicate graph registrations silently render blank or select the first definition
root_cause: The controller accepts any string; graph addition never enforces uniqueness; host dispatch uses find and nullable lets without an error branch.
impact: Route typos or restoring a removed route leave a blank host. Duplicate registrations silently prefer the first definition, concealing graph construction errors.
recommendation: Validate graph uniqueness, define unknown-route behavior and restoration migrations, and provide a visible/fail-fast diagnostic appropriate to debug versus production. Keep registration/entry lookup consistent with the chosen controller architecture.
risks: A controller can be used before a host attaches; validation must not accidentally prohibit legitimate graph initialization or typed-route migrations.
required_tests: Duplicate route registration produces a deterministic diagnostic.
Navigate/start/restore with an unknown route has explicit behavior and no silent blank screen.
Restore a route removed by an app upgrade using the documented fallback.

title: Navigation exposes two incompatible controller abstractions and lacks a declared platform capability contract
root_cause: The expect NavHostController is AndroidX on Android and Adaptive elsewhere, while the public rememberNavController and AdaptiveNavHost use Adaptive on every platform. Non-Android AndroidBackHandler actuals are no-ops and no browser/native stack adapter exists.
impact: Consumers may assume AndroidX lifecycle/back-stack ownership, iOS native interactive gestures or browser history support that the Adaptive API does not implement. The module is included but intentionally not published and was described as coming soon.
recommendation: Keep navigation experimental/unpublished. Record an ADR selecting an adapter to a mature navigation library or a deliberately minimal independent stack; publish an explicit capability matrix and an API migration plan before implementation.
risks: A rewrite during identity migration would create unnecessary compatibility and licensing risk. No-op platform behavior is source-confirmed, but absence of a promised advanced feature is tracked as an improvement rather than an invented runtime vulnerability.
required_tests: Compile a common consumer using the supported controller factory/host API on every target.
Android system/predictive back, iOS app-provided back/gesture behavior, desktop keyboard back and web history are tested according to the declared contract.
Per-entry lifecycle/viewmodel/restoration requirements are specified before release.

title: CupertinoIcon leaves the private-use glyph Text semantics exposed
root_cause: The icon is a Material Text displaying a private-use character. A null contentDescription adds no semantics modifier, leaving the Text node; a non-null description adds parent image semantics without clearing the child text semantics.
impact: Decorative icons are not reliably excluded from accessibility output, and labeled icons can retain a meaningless glyph-text node. The source-level semantics issue is confirmed; exact VoiceOver/TalkBack utterances and merged-node behavior were not executed here.
recommendation: Implement explicit decorative-versus-labeled icon semantics, suppressing the glyph Text semantics while retaining one meaningful image description where provided. Follow Compose semantics guidance and test both merged/unmerged trees and real assistive technology.
risks: Unconditionally clearing outer semantics could erase a caller's click action or label. Font glyph presence tests do not establish accessibility correctness.
required_tests: A null-description icon contributes no readable PUA text semantics.
A labeled icon contributes one image label and no additional glyph announcement.
Icons inside buttons preserve the button action/label in merged and unmerged trees.
Run TalkBack, VoiceOver and desktop/browser accessibility checks at different font scales.

title: Generated icon/symbol catalogues lack a reproducible generator and Apple availability metadata
root_cause: Generated declarations claim SF/Cupertino coverage but the repository contains no generator/source manifest capable of reproducing names, aliases, categories and version mapping. SF names cover versions1.0-7.0 without per-symbol minimum-OS/variant/fallback metadata.
impact: Future updates cannot be mechanically reviewed against a canonical source, and newer Apple names may resolve to no system image on older supported OS versions. This is not proof of an unconditional crash: the underlying UIImage lookup is nullable.
recommendation: Store generator code, pinned permitted input provenance and deterministic outputs; keep Cupertino font and Apple system name catalogues distinct. Add per-symbol availability or documented fallback/feature detection at the UIKit boundary.
risks: Apple artwork licensing is separate from identifier strings. Font/codepoint validation proves mapping consistency, not glyph meaning, visual layout or OS availability of SF names.

Retain checks for unique identifiers, aliases, valid referenced names and cmap coverage.

title: Sample secure password text field logs every entered value
root_cause: The password example sets isSecure=true but its onValueChange prints "Password: $it". The adjacent name field also prints user-entered text.
impact: Real values entered into the demonstration can appear in local/device diagnostic output; copying the example propagates an unsafe pattern. This is a local logging exposure, not evidence of remote exfiltration or an embedded secret.
recommendation: Remove value logging from secure/user-data examples. If feedback is useful, display a non-sensitive event/count and explicitly teach that secure rendering does not make logging safe.
risks: Verification must use synthetic test strings, never an owner's actual password or log dump. Avoid overclassifying a demo log as a remote attack.
required_tests: Type a synthetic password and confirm its bytes never appear in captured test logs.
Source assertion prevents interpolation of secure-field content into logging calls.
Verify secure keyboard/display behavior separately on an iOS device.

title: Sample image export runs unbounded reads and image allocations without error or concurrency control
root_cause: The export click launches in the composition scope, reads the entire file before switching to Default, then fully decodes/crops/encodes with no size/dimension cap, busy guard or exception handler. Android/JVM/iOS readByteArray actuals perform synchronous I/O. Non-Android encoding force-unwraps nullable data; selected images are all composed in a scrolling Column.
impact: Large/corrupt/inaccessible inputs can freeze UI work, fail the coroutine or require several simultaneous full-size buffers; rapid clicks duplicate work. OOM magnitude and Skia resource lifetime are risks needing profiling, not measured leaks in this audit. Large multi-selection can also create excessive concurrent image work.
recommendation: Separate I/O/CPU dispatch appropriately, bound input and decoded dimensions, downsample before crop, serialize/cancel exports, surface recoverable errors and retain CancellationException. Check encoder success/null results and deterministic release of owned native resources. Use a lazy bounded image list.
risks: Dispatchers.Default is not a universal nonblocking-I/O guarantee, especially in browsers. Do not close Compose-owned bitmaps accidentally. Picker/saver native resource bugs are covered by the I/O audit rather than duplicated here.
required_tests: Corrupt/empty/revoked/large-dimension images fail gracefully without crashing or leaking handles.
Rapid repeated export and navigation away cancel/serialize work correctly.
Measure peak memory and UI responsiveness on representative Android/iOS/JVM devices and browsers.
Encoder failure and multi-select hundreds-of-images paths have bounded work and lazy rendering.

title: Streaming sample cancellation does not interrupt its synchronous read loop
root_cause: Replacing a selection cancels the old job, but countBytes loops over synchronous RawSource reads without suspension or checking coroutine cancellation. withContext(Default) and catching/rethrowing CancellationException do not inject a check inside that loop.
impact: A cancelled or no-longer-visible sample operation can continue consuming CPU/storage until EOF or I/O failure. The surrounding use correctly closes the source on exit; this finding is delayed cancellation, not a confirmed never-close leak.
recommendation: Make the loop cancellation-cooperative with an explicit coroutine-context check per bounded chunk and test with a deliberately slow source. Document that the browser RawSource path currently buffers the whole Blob before the sample loop; fixed read chunks do not make that platform constant-memory.
risks: An OS read may itself be uninterruptible; checking before chunks limits delay but is not a hard real-time cancellation guarantee. Browser buffering belongs to the I/O implementation audit.
required_tests: Slow fake source counts reads after cancellation and proves prompt termination/close.
Reselect a file and leave the screen while counting; old work stops and does not overwrite new results.
Run large native/JVM input with a defined cancellation latency bound.
Correct sample memory claims for JS/Wasm buffering.

title: Android sample permission menu and manifest disagree and declare unrelated broad permissions
root_cause: The menu requests Permission.Call, mapped to CALL_PHONE, but the sample manifest never declares CALL_PHONE. Conversely it declares MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and READ/SEND/RECEIVE_SMS without a corresponding special-access workflow/SMS demo in this sample.
impact: The Call permission example cannot demonstrate a normal grant for the declared app. Broad/unrelated declarations mislead integrators and can impose distribution-policy scrutiny; a declaration alone does not grant access or establish a security vulnerability.
recommendation: Align explicit demonstration scenarios and merged manifests; remove unrelated permissions or split narrowly scoped demo variants. Teach special-access APIs separately from ordinary runtime permissions. Keep Android SDK/version constraints and iOS usage keys in the permission module's test matrix.
risks: Do not add sensitive permissions to a general sample merely to make all status rows turn green. FileProvider is nonexported and uses grantUriPermissions; its cache path is not evidence of universally exposed storage.
required_tests: Inspect the merged manifest and map every menu permission to its expected declaration/status for supported API levels.
Test Call on a fresh installation under an explicitly approved demo variant.
Verify file/image picker operation without MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and unrelated SMS permissions.
Run permission denial/permanent-denial and Android13/14 media-selection scenarios.
